data.body: The job's permissions are still `contents: read` + `pull-requests: write` only, but `scripts/pr_status_labels.py`'s `ensure_review_label()` creates the repository's `needs-review` label via `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels` whenever it doesn't already exist. GitHub's REST API requires the **Issues** repository permission (write) to create a repository-level label definition; `pull-requests: write` only authorizes adding/removing an *existing* label on a specific issue/PR number (`POST`/`DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/labels...`), which accepts either `issues:write` or `pull-requests:write`, but label *creation* has no such pull-requests fallback. Because `needs-review` is a brand-new label that won't pre-exist in any consuming repository (including this one, per `docs/pr-status-labels.md`), the very first qualifying run (`opened`/`reopened`/`ready_for_review` from a non-writer author, or any `changes-requested` flip) will fail at `ensure_review_label()` with `Resource not accessible by integration`; `main()` catches the error and returns 1 before any label is applied, so the feature never fires. Add `issues: write` to this job's `permissions` block (and update the matching comment, the usage snippet and security-model text in `docs/pr-status-labels.md`, and the `test_token_can_only_read_contents_and_write_pull_requests` assertion that currently forbids `issues: write`), or pre-create the `needs-review` label out of band in every consuming repository and drop the auto-create path from `ensure_review_label()`.
